questions.q: Why doesn't a successful imperative Apex write automatically refresh a separately wired custom Apex read?
options: Because imperative calls are always slower than wired calls
Because the wire service has no way to know that an unrelated imperative call changed the data it is caching
Because wired reads are refreshed only once per day by the platform
Because imperative calls are not allowed to modify any data a wire adapter depends on
questions.explain: The wire service caches results for the specific configuration it was given; it has no visibility into an entirely separate imperative call changing the underlying data, which is exactly the gap refreshApex() and notifyRecordUpdateAvailable() exist to close.

questions.q: What must a component store from its wired Apex function in order for `refreshApex()` to work correctly?
options: Only the data property of the result
Only the error property of the result
The entire result object the wire function receives, containing both data and error
Nothing needs to be stored; refreshApex() works automatically on any wired property
questions.explain: refreshApex() needs the whole object the wire function received (both data and error) to know what configuration to re-fetch. Storing only result.data is a common mistake that breaks the refresh silently.

options: Re-running a wired custom Apex method's configuration, bypassing its cache
Telling LDS to refresh its cache for specific record Ids across every component using those records through getRecord
Deleting a record and all of its child records
Subscribing a component to a Lightning Message Channel
questions.explain: notifyRecordUpdateAvailable() is used when an LDS-managed record changes through something other than LDS itself (such as a custom Apex update) -- it tells LDS to refresh its cache for that record everywhere it's wired.

questions.q: What is the current guidance regarding `getRecordNotifyChange()`?
options: It is the current recommended function and should always be used instead of notifyRecordUpdateAvailable()
It is deprecated; notifyRecordUpdateAvailable() is the current replacement, and it considers record data wired by all instantiated components
It was removed from the platform entirely and no longer exists in any form
It performs the exact same role as refreshApex(), just with a different name
questions.explain: getRecordNotifyChange() is deprecated. notifyRecordUpdateAvailable() is the current replacement and has broader behavior, considering record data wired by all instantiated components rather than the narrower deprecated call.

questions.q: If a record changes entirely through LDS itself (e.g. via updateRecord), what additional refresh step is needed for other components with that record wired via getRecord?
options: refreshApex() must be called manually
notifyRecordUpdateAvailable() must be called manually
Nothing extra is needed -- LDS's own shared cache already keeps every component wired to that record in sync automatically
Every component must be reloaded from scratch
questions.explain: When a change goes entirely through LDS, LDS's shared cache already propagates the update to every component wired to that record -- the extra refresh tools in this lesson are specifically for changes that happen outside LDS's own write path.
